producer_report.summary: When the reader gives no reading, its error is now committed with the failed-reading record and printed on the drain line for the item. An unread job is now read once more, and if that also fails the drain skips the item with its reason and runs the next one. The skip does not set the repeated-failure stop. Root cause, in two places. (1) reading.rs built the failed-reading commit without the error that `read_for` returned, so `Proposal.reader_error` never reached the commit. A new `failed_reading_body` adds "The reader gave no usable reading: <error>" (redacted, one line, cut to 1000 chars; a fixed "withheld" text if redaction fails) to the body in `first_reading` and in `correct`. (2) `go_job` bailed for a Proposed job with no reading, so the drain's second attempt failed too and RepeatedFailure fired. That arm now calls the new `read_unread` and returns `GoResult::Reread`. The re-read takes `next_seq()` for the invocation, commits "Read a request again (the reader failed)" or "Read a request again: <title>", and writes no new request record. In drain.rs a queued, not-pre-read job whose read gave a job id plus an error returns the new `RunStep::Unread`. `attempts` counts those apart from `failures`: the first loops for the re-read and the second ends as the new `ItemEnd::Skipped`, with a note naming the reason. `finish` sets no stop for Skipped. `push` shows `: <reason>` only for the "not read" outcome. Retries and failures after a read keep the old path. Tests: two athena-core pin tests (error text in the commit body; `go` re-reads with distinct invocation seqs 1, 2, 3) and two drain tests with the real steps (re-read then skip with the error in the log and the commits, the reader called twice and the next item landed; a re-read that succeeds runs the item). A CHANGELOG entry is under Unreleased / Fixed.

open_issues: `athena go <id>` on an unread Proposed job now reads it again and spends reader budget, where it used to print a hint about `athena correct`. This is the same behavior as `go` on a Queued job. The reader's per-job budget check still applies.
I did not check main.rs for how an `athena go` re-read that fails again shows the reader error; the same `GoResult::Reread` path serves a Queued job.
The drain's Stop::RepeatedFailure 'meaning' string is unchanged ('the same item failed twice; the item is named'). Only the doc comment now says unread items are skipped instead.
mistakes: I first made `Proposal.spent_usd` for a re-read include the job's earlier spend. That would have made the drain count the first read's cost twice. I fixed it before any test run so a re-read reports only its own cost.
My first drain test asserted Stop::QueueEmpty; the real stop is TargetMet. I corrected the assertion.
learnings: `Proposal.spent_usd` holds the cost of the read just made in the `ask`, queued-read and re-read paths, and the drain adds it to its spend. A re-read must not add the earlier read's cost again. `correct` is the exception: it includes the job's earlier spend.

A job with invocations and no readings is JobState::Proposed (`Queued` needs no invocations either), and `read_once` numbers its snapshot and reading n from the readings, so a re-read of an unread job uses n=1 with a new invocation seq.

With the fake agent, setting `turn.structured = None` for the reader gives the single-call failure 'the reader returned no structured reading'. A refused reading would run the reader twice in one read, so it would hide whether the drain re-read.
The drain tests' rated scenario sets a final stop of TargetMet when a later item lands. A drain test that skips one item and lands another therefore ends TargetMet, not QueueEmpty.
